questionText:
Consider the following definition of a lexical token id for an identifier in a programming language, using extended regular expressions:

$$\begin{array}{lcl} \text{letter} & \rightarrow & [\text{A-Za-z}] \\ \text{digit} & \rightarrow & [0-9] \\ \text{id} & \rightarrow & \text{letter } (\text{letter} \mid \text{digit})^* \end{array}$$

Which one of the following Non-deterministic Finite-state Automata with $\epsilon$-transitions accepts the set of valid identifiers? (A double-circle denotes a final state)
explanation:
Step 1: Analyze the Regular Expression
The regular expression given for an identifier is:
$$\text{id} \rightarrow \text{letter} (\text{letter} \mid \text{digit})^*$$
This means an identifier must begin with a $\text{letter}$, followed by zero or more repetitions of either a $\text{letter}$ or a $\text{digit}$.

Step 2: Thompson's Construction for $\epsilon$-NFA
1. Processing the initial $\text{letter}$ moves from the start state to a state that is marked as a final state (accepting a single-letter identifier).
2. To handle $(\text{letter} \mid \text{digit})^*$, standard Thompson's construction for Kleene star and union is applied:
- $\epsilon$-transitions split into two parallel branches: one for $\text{letter}$ and one for $\text{digit}$.
- After consuming $\text{letter}$ or $\text{digit}$, $\epsilon$-transitions merge into a single state.
- An $\epsilon$-transition loops back from this state to repeat, and another $\epsilon$-transition allows bypassing or reaching the final accepting state.

Step 3: Conclusion
Option (C) correctly matches the structural $\epsilon$-NFA diagram obtained via Thompson's construction for $(\text{letter} \mid \text{digit})^*$ following the initial $\text{letter}$.

Hence, the correct option is C.
